audit: Data-integrity problems: 52 mutation rows are internally impossible: missense changes that no single-nucleotide substitution can produce (e.g. M>Y, W>N) and/or protein positions far beyond the protein's length (e.g. NOTCH2 p.E127469G, BCOR p.K110637W, NF2 p.P21404E). They cluster entirely in four gene-diagnosis pairs - NOTCH2 in embryonal RMS, BCOR in medulloblastoma, MED12 in ependymoma, NF2 in pilocytic astrocytoma - which were among the strongest 'novel' signals before QC; remaining rows in those pairs also show positions exceeding the protein length or random-looking substitutions, so I treat all four as injected/corrupted and report none of them (BCOR in SHH medulloblastoma is real biology, but this cohort's evidence for it is corrupt). Other concerns: ~19 hypermutated tumours (>200 mutations, up to 15,731; likely MMR/POLE) were excluded as they generate spurious long-gene hits; recurrent non-hotspot variants seen across unrelated diagnoses (C17orf80 p.S281R x72, HLTF p.Q898E, ZNF510 p.Q248E, CD69, CD46, ABCF1 p.P9L, PPP4R3A p.L174Q) look like germline/pipeline artifacts; several identical single-mutation profiles across cases; diagnosis labels are heterogeneous and nested (NOS vs subtype, 'missing', 'Unknown', 'Neoplasm, NOS'), many rare diagnoses have <10 cases; WES misses fusions and deletions (e.g. KIAA1549-BRAF, SMARCB1 deletions) so frequencies are underestimates; BRAF V600E appears as p.V640E (alternate transcript). After QC I found no novel association I would put in a paper: every surviving candidate outside known biology rests on 2-5 mutated cases, is not significant after burden adjustment and multiple testing across ~900 tests, or is a long/passenger gene. All reported claims are established drivers; I deliberately did not pad the list with novel-looking noise despite the request for ten-plus new findings.
methods: Excluded 52 biologically impossible mutation rows and 19 hypermutated cases (>200 non-synonymous mutations). For each diagnosis x gene (gene mutated in >=3 cases, >=2 in the diagnosis) I counted mutated cases and ran a one-sided Fisher exact test versus all other cases, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, plus a burden-adjusted Poisson-binomial test in which each case's mutation probability scales with its total mutation count. I inspected hotspot structure, variant classes and per-row plausibility for top hits, then kept associations with strong statistics and coherent mutation patterns; probabilities reflect statistical strength, sample size and prior biological knowledge, and expected frequencies are observed rates shrunk modestly.
